# Client-local shadow validation of heterogeneous model transfer

Use the existing P13 learner-disjoint development cohort. Among all earlier learner IDs assign a common SHA-256 bucket (first four bytes of the digest of "shadow-v1:" followed by the deidentified decimal learner number). Residues 0–1 modulo 5 supply earlier calibration registrations. Fit only on remaining earlier registrations. The already inspected 2014J cohort supplies development outcomes. Use the existing .02 macro-course AUC gain screen and simultaneous 95% intervals. Measure per-course calibration, tenth-percentile course AUC, and fraction of courses whose AUC is lower than local-only. Units are course modules at one institution.

Assign alternating modules, in name order, to logistic and single-hidden-layer (16 tanh units) models. Train both alternatives for each module with common fixed seed 73. Generate 512 deterministic synthetic anchor activity vectors respecting count constraints without inspecting any case features. Each module publishes its frozen model's withdrawal probability vector on the anchors. Supply the equal average of *other modules'* vectors to the recipient. For the distillation branch fine-tune its original model with equal local-label and anchor cross-entropy. The matched local branch takes as many optimizer updates on local labels. This one-round FedMD-style transfer uses public synthetic anchors in place of auxiliary student records. Compare all-logistic and all-MLP rosters to the alternating roster. Fit identical methods centrally for reference.

Calibrate local and transferred probability logits by separately fitting a local intercept on held-out earlier learners. Divide each course's calibration learners into three risk strata using tertiles of its calibrated local forecast (implemented by within-course registration quantiles). In each stratum select a convex transfer weight in {0,.25,.5,.75,1} minimizing summed log loss plus 64 times mean all-calibration loss in that course. Tie-break toward less transfer. Apply those cutoffs and weights to development predictions. Controls include no transfer, full transfer, fixed half, a single locally validated weight, and the same gate with local calibration removed. Report homogeneous rosters with the same gate, as well as fixed FedAvg/FedProx and weak-ridge local adaptation on the fitting partition. Re-score the earlier full-training benchmark separately; its larger training set and different payload are relevant. Conditional inference over learners covers the observed seven courses and fixed seed. This is a development screen.
